en: The Philippine Declaration of Independence was signed by 98 delegates on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Philippine Congress has two chambers: a Senate with 24 members and a House of Representatives with over 300 members.
Jose Rizal published Noli Me Tangere at age 26 and El Filibusterismo at age 31 to inspire Filipino nationalism.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct native languages, but Filipino and English serve as the two official languages.
Cebu's Sinulog Festival happens every third Sunday of January, attracting millions of visitors to watch the street dances.
The Ifugao indigenous people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over 2,000 years ago using simple tools.
The Sampaguita, the national flower, has 5 to 9 white petals and was declared the national flower in 1934.
Dr. Fe del Mundo founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines in 1957 after studying at Harvard.
Under Philippine election laws, citizens must be at least 18 years old to register and vote in elections.
Andres Bonifacio founded the secret Katipunan society in 1892, which eventually grew to over 100,000 members.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the 9-meter-tall Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan to honor Andres Bonifacio and other revolutionaries.
The Philippine archipelago is politically divided into 81 provinces, which are organized into 17 distinct administrative regions.
